subject: general
question: In reproductive health, the aim of contraception is _________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**to prevent unplanned pregnancies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Contraception** refers to methods or devices used to prevent pregnancy during sexual activity. It allows individuals or couples to plan and control the timing and number of their children.
 
• The primary aim of contraception is **to prevent unplanned pregnancies**, ensuring that families can make informed decisions about parenthood. *Hence, this statement is correct.*
 
• Contraception is a significant part of **reproductive health**, promoting physical, emotional, and economic well-being by allowing spacing or limiting the number of children.
 
• It also helps in reducing the **risk of maternal and child mortality**, as planned pregnancies are generally safer for both the mother and child.
 
• Various methods of contraception include **barrier methods** (e.g., condoms), **hormonal methods** (e.g., birth control pills), **intrauterine devices (IUDs)**, and **permanent methods** like sterilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Importance of Contraception:**

 
 
• It helps in controlling the **global population growth**, which is crucial for sustainable development and resource management.
 
• Contraception reduces the risk of **sexually transmitted infections (STIs)** like HIV when barrier methods such as condoms are used.
 
• It prevents **teenage pregnancies**, enabling young individuals to complete their education and achieve their career goals.
 
• Family planning through contraception contributes to **gender equality**, as it empowers women to take control of their reproductive health.
 
 
 
• **Popular Contraceptive Methods and Their Features:**
 
 
• **Barrier Methods:** Includes condoms and diaphragms; these are physical devices that block sperm from reaching the egg.
 
• **Hormonal Methods:** Includes oral contraceptive pills, patches, and injections; these regulate hormones to prevent ovulation.
 
• **Intrauterine Devices (IUDs):** T-shaped devices inserted into the uterus to prevent pregnancy; they can be hormonal or copper-based.
 
• **Permanent Methods:** Includes surgical procedures like vasectomy (for males) and tubal ligation (for females) for irreversible contraception.
 
 
 
• **Unplanned Pregnancies:**
 
 
• An unplanned pregnancy occurs when a pregnancy is unintended at the time of conception.
 
• According to the **World Health Organization (WHO)**, approximately **121 million unintended pregnancies** occur globally each year.
 
• Unplanned pregnancies can result in **health complications**, financial burdens, and emotional stress for individuals or families.
 
 
 
• **Global Initiatives:**
 
 
• The **Family Planning 2020 (FP2020)** initiative aims to expand access to contraceptives globally, particularly in developing countries.
 
• The Indian government promotes contraception through its **National Family Planning Programme**, which offers free or subsidized contraceptive methods to the population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** "To have more babies" is incorrect as contraception is designed to prevent pregnancy, not facilitate it.
 
• **Option 2:** "To prevent unplanned pregnancies" is correct as the primary purpose of contraception is to allow individuals to plan for pregnancy. *Hence, this is the correct answer.*
 
• **Option 3:** "To make babies healthy" is incorrect as contraception does not directly influence the health of babies; it prevents pregnancies instead.
 
• **Option 4:** "To make twin babies" is incorrect as contraception does not determine the number of babies conceived.
 
 
 
• Contraception is a critical tool in achieving public health goals such as reducing maternal mortality, preventing unsafe abortions, and improving family welfare.
